subject: Reschedule: Cross-region product demo — holiday windows & DST coordination
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Oct 2024 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Demo availability — Redwood inference (30–45min)

Hi Aiko / Priya / Liam,

Thanks for the interest — excited to show a short walkthrough of Redwood Inference and cover fit for your latency/cost questions. To avoid the usual timezone traps I pulled a couple of slots that try to line up US / EU / APAC overlap windows. Please pick anything that works or propose alternatives: 

- Option A: Tue Nov 5, 09:00 PT (Tue Nov 5, 17:00 CET / Wed Nov 6, 01:00 JST)
- Option B: Fri Nov 8, 16:00 UTC (Fri Nov 8, 17:00 CET / Sat Nov 9, 01:00 JST)
- Option C: Mon Nov 11, 17:00 IST (Mon Nov 11, 12:30 UTC / Mon Nov 11, 21:30 JST)

A couple of notes that caused me to avoid some earlier slots: daylight savings in the EU ends the week of Oct 27 which will shift CET/CEST alignment vs US; Diwali falls early-November this year for many India teams, and Japan has Culture Day and a couple of local holidays in early November too. We typically avoid Golden Week in May and Easter bank holidays in April for repeat scheduling.

I've attached an .ics with Option B as a placeholder and a short timezone chart. If none of those work, tell me: (1) your best 2-hour window in local time; (2) whether you prefer a recording only vs live.

Thanks — Marissa

[Attachment: invite.ics (calendar invite)]
[Attachment: timezones-chart.png]

Subject: Re: Demo availability — Redwood inference (30–45min)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks — appreciate the explicit windowing. A few quick points from the Japan side:
- Culture Day (Nov 3) is a national holiday and several engineers will be OOO around that date.
- Golden Week is in May (I know you mentioned it as a recurring constraint); we generally avoid early-May demos when possible.

Of your options, Option B (Fri Nov 8, 16:00 UTC) looks workable for us — that would be 01:00 JST if I read that right, which is late but some folks can join if the core team can shift. Option C in IST is very late for Japan.

One ask: please confirm whether the calendar invite includes UTC and the localized times. We've had invites shift on accept when the organizer's calendar is set to PDT vs UTC — makes a mess with daylight savings.

Best,
Aiko

Hi all,

EU side is flexible but a few operational notes:
- DST in Europe ends on Oct 27 this year, so any recurring invites created before then can show a one-hour shift for attendees in Europe if the organizer's calendar is on PDT.
- We also try to avoid the week before Easter (bank holidays across countries vary) for planning future demos.

Option B (Nov 8, 16:00 UTC) is fine for me. If others prefer Nov 18 week, that also works.

Cheers,
Liam

2) I'll create the invite with explicit timezone labels and include the .ics as UTC-based. Please accept only after verifying the localized time shown in your calendar client.
3) If Nov 8 still doesn't work for someone, fallback: Mon Nov 18, 09:00 UTC.
